title: Unit-compatible comparison of universal arrows in a quasicategory
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces, homotopy fibers and equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a universe containing all the simplicial sets below. Let $R:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor, let $d\in\mathcal D$, and let $a,a'\in\mathcal C$ carry arrows $\eta:d\to R(a)$ and $\eta':d\to R(a')$. Suppose that, for every $c\in\mathcal C$, both maps
$$\Phi_c:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(a,c)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(d,R(c)),\quad h\mapsto R(h)\circ\eta,$$
$$\Phi'_c:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(a',c)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(d,R(c)),\quad h\mapsto R(h)\circ\eta'$$
are equivalences. Then the homotopy fiber $\operatorname{hofib}_{\eta'}(\Phi_{a'})$, the space of pairs $(\beta:a\to a',\,R(\beta)\circ\eta\simeq\eta')$, is contractible, and every such $\beta$ is an equivalence in $\mathcal C$. In particular there exist $\gamma:a'\to a$ and homotopies $R(\gamma)\circ\eta'\simeq\eta$, $\gamma\beta\simeq\mathrm{id}_a$ and $\beta\gamma\simeq\mathrm{id}_{a'}$. No functorial variation of $a,a'$ or adjoint to $R$ is assumed.

source.place: Agent-formulated universal-arrow comparison extracted from the unit-compatibility argument for Gepner--Haugseng Lemma A.4.7. Kerodon Corollary 4.7.3.14 (02HM), read online, supplies the supporting uniqueness principle for initial objects, not this exact comma/mapping-space formulation. WANTED: an archived proof of the stated universal-arrow comparison. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], the right-pinched mapping spaces of $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ are Kan complexes in the containing universe. Apply [lem-coef-space-contractible-fiber-equivalence] to the assumed equivalence $\Phi_{a'}$ and the vertex $\eta'$. Its homotopy fiber is contractible. By the path-fiber definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], its vertices are exactly the pairs $(\beta,H)$ with $\beta:a\to a'$ and $H:R(\beta)\circ\eta\simeq\eta'$, with the full higher path data retained. In particular this space is nonempty: a weak equivalence to a point is bijective on components, so its realization is nonempty and hence it has a vertex. Fix any such pair; the remaining argument applies to every pair, not just a chosen preferred comparison.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: agent expansion of unit-compatible universal-arrow comparison, beneath the finite-coefficient adjunction

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-space-contractible-fiber-equivalence] also to $\Phi'_a$ and the vertex $\eta$. Choose a vertex of this contractible fiber as in Step 1. It supplies $\gamma:a'\to a$ and $H':R(\gamma)\circ\eta'\simeq\eta$. Work on components of the Kan mapping spaces. By [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] these components form the ordinary homotopy categories $h\mathcal C$ and $h\mathcal D$, with associative composition and identities. The simplicial functor $R$ preserves this composition: apply $R$ to a $2$-simplex witnessing a composite, and use the cited node's $2$-simplex composition rule; it also preserves degenerate identity edges. The assumptions on $\Phi_a$ and $\Phi'_{a'}$ imply that their induced functions on components are injective, by the definition of weak equivalence. Here the two compatibility paths give $[R\beta][\eta]=[\eta']$ and $[R\gamma][\eta']=[\eta]$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: agent expansion of unit-compatible universal-arrow comparison, beneath the finite-coefficient adjunction

proof.text:
Compute in $h\mathcal D$, using associativity, units and the functoriality established in Step 2:
$$[\Phi_a(\gamma\beta)]=[R\gamma][R\beta][\eta]=[R\gamma][\eta']=[\eta]=[\Phi_a(1_a)].$$
Injectivity of $\pi_0\Phi_a$ gives $[\gamma][\beta]=[1_a]$ in $h\mathcal C$. Similarly
$$[\Phi'_{a'}(\beta\gamma)]=[R\beta][R\gamma][\eta']=[R\beta][\eta]=[\eta']=[\Phi'_{a'}(1_{a'})],$$
so injectivity of $\pi_0\Phi'_{a'}$ gives $[\beta][\gamma]=[1_{a'}]$. These are calculations with the specified unit paths, not cancellation of $R$ as a faithful functor. The compositions and their component interpretation are those of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition].

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: agent expansion of unit-compatible universal-arrow comparison, beneath the finite-coefficient adjunction

proof.text: Thus $[\beta]$ is invertible in $h\mathcal C$, with inverse $[\gamma]$. The equivalence-edge criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] makes $\beta$ an equivalence in $\mathcal C$. The component equalities just proved give homotopies $\gamma\beta\simeq1_a$ and $\beta\gamma\simeq1_{a'}$: in a Kan mapping space, vertices in the same component are joined by an edge, since horns compose successive edges and reverse edges. Together with $H'$ and the original $H$ this is all the asserted data. Since $(\beta,H)$ was arbitrary, every comparison is an equivalence, and Step 1 already proved contractibility of the entire comparison space. Nothing here assembles $a,a'$ as functors or assumes an adjoint to $R$.
